old_title: Hull City v Brighton: Premier League - live
new_title: Hull City 2-0 Brighton: Premier League - as it happened
old_text:
33 mins: Rutter isn't a regular starter for Brighton, especially not in the No 9 position and I wonder whether the Seagulls are missing having an out-and-out striker. Rutter, Gomez, Gross and Ayari ... they all kind of prefer playing in the pocket. Maybe a focal point would benefit Brighton instead.
32 mins: Cho gets a rare opportunity to run at Costinha and gets in a cross with his left foot, which Matt Crooks tries to flick from behind him. Unfortunately for Hull, Crooks cannot get any power on the flick and it's straight at Verbruggen.
Tzolakis parries from Rutter at the other end, another smart save from the Hull stopper.
28 mins: A well co-ordinated press from Hull has Verbruggen and his defenders worrying for a moment, hurriedly squirrelling the ball into touch, which allows another long throw from the hosts. Mendy hooks it tamely at the Brighton goal, and Verbruggen collects.
23 mins: Some really strong and determined play from Iroegbunam earns his team a free-kick. The referee tried to play an advantage for Hull before bringing the play back.
Is this worth a shot? Slater and Belloumi stand over it.
21 mins: Another chance for Brighton, this time Ayari picking up the headed knockdown from Rutter and scuffing his effort, which means it's an easy save for Tzolakis.
20 mins: Brighton are starting to tick here. Their short passing, their movement, their invention ... it's all superb to watch. A fluid move ends with Costinha having a shot, but he guides it wide. That was another big chance.
18 mins: A deflection runs kindly for Gomez down the right and then Rutter gets it wrong in taking the return away from his teammate. Brighton keep the pressure on, before Costinha's cross is held by Tzolakis.
17 mins: Ironic cheers from the home fans as their team get a free-kick. Slater bundled over. Brighton have been fairly spiky in their tackling so far, and perhaps the Hull fans felt that free-kick was overdue.
A huge save from Tzolakis! That looked goal bound. It was De Cuyper whose low cross from the left was brilliantly precise, and Gomez should probably have finished it off. The Hull keeper made himself big to deny the Paraguayan at close range.
14 mins: Both keepers have had crosses to catch and errant through-balls to collect, but we haven't really had a shot in anger yet. Gomez drills in a powerful cross low from the right but nobody in a Brighton shirt is anywhere near it.
13 mins: Brighton are actually playing more on the counterattack at the moment, which isn't quite what I envisaged for this match, against the low-blockers of Hull City.
Boscagli's speculative cross does not find Rutter.
8 mins: Brighton are finally getting into it, pushing Hull back with a prolonged period of possession. The black and amber shirts are shuttling back and forth to keep the visitors chanceless, at the moment. Good disciplined defence.
6 mins: Hull's shape does resemble more of a 4-3-3, or 4-5-1, with Cho and Belloumi being asked to get forward into wide positions and support McBurnie. The home team have started confidently.
4 mins: Rutter and Gomez link up nicely down Brighton's inside-right channel but Tzolakis is there to catch the former's cutback. Nice pacy start to the game, this.
2 mins: Brighton's press baiting play deep in possession might not be so successful against a Hull team who are happy to sit in a low block, even at home. But the home side have come out quite aggressively, with Regan Slater barging into Diego Gomez to concede a free-kick.
Some important pre-match news for me personally ... my significant other has brought a tube of sour cream and onion Pringles into my home office. Huge. Absolutely elite live blogging snack. Less than 10 minutes until KO now.
Fabian Hürzeler sounded a little way of Hull in his pre-match press conference, citing the Tigers' narrow 1-0 defeat to table-topping (and possible title rivals) Arsenal as a template for how today's game might go.
"I think they do an impressive job," Hürzeler said. "They had a brilliant start in the Premier League. They are very structured. Against Arsenal, I think Arsenal suffered. They [Arsenal] didn't create a lot of big chances, and therefore we need to be patient because we also know that Hull are really good in transition.
"They also have individual quality in their team. Very well structured, very well organised, good in transition, good in set pieces, and I think it's not an easy place to go to."
Hull obviously beat Manchester United 2-0 in their opening home game and have drawn four successive matches at the MKM Stadium since, so that proves Hürzeler's point somewhat.
Women's Super League: Both Manchester clubs are in serious danger of suffering shock defeats in the early WSL games this afternoon. The two matches are approaching their denouement, so catch the latest with Emillia Hawkins on our clockwatch blog.
My personal two-pennies-worth is that Brighton will probably fall away from the title race at some stage after Christmas. Their fixture list in the short term is fairly inviting, so I see their lofty position being sustained for a little while.
But realistically, a top five finish and Champions League qualification should be their primary objective. That's really not impossible when you consider the struggles of Manchester United and Chelsea, and the possible fate of Manchester City if and when a verdict/punishment arrives re their 115s charges.
The fact Fabian Hürzeler could achieve that just after his 34th birthday would be an astonishing feat in itself.
The stats don't lie when it comes to Brighton's brilliant form. They are well clear as the Premier League's top scorers with 26, despite many of their rivals having played a game more. They are also level with Arsenal (7) in terms of goals conceded, again having played fewer games than the Gunners.
Pascal Gross also leads way in the league this season for chances created (29).
They don't have one outstanding goalscorer, but Gross is on four so far this season, with Yasin Ayari, Jack Hinshelwood and Charalampos Kostoulas all chipping in with three.
There's plenty of time before kick-off to get around this special report on Brighton's superb start to the season by William Ralston. In it, he analyses exactly what the Seagulls have excelled in so far, what comes next and their chances of remaining in the title hunt in the coming months and weeks.
Go inside a brilliantly run club who are upsetting the traditional Premier League big six:
It looks like Hull could line up in a 4-4-2 today. It remains to be seen where Mohamed-Ali Cho will play, either on one of the flanks or pushed up alongside Oliver McBurnie. Mohamed Belloumi has been their primary creator this season, so watch out for him.
Brighton will surely shape up in their standard 4-2-3-1 formation, fluid as that is, with the likes of Diego Gomez, Yasin Ayari and Pascal Gross rotating between the midfield lines.
Peter Bankes (from Merseyside) is the referee today, with Andrew Kitchen in the VAR booth.
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the solitary early kick-off in the Premier League today. Many will view Hull City versus Brighton as a mere hors d'oeuvres to the main dish of Liverpool against Manchester United later, but there is plenty riding on it.
Hull have not won a game in any competition since claiming back-to-back victories in a shock opening burst after winning promotion, while Brighton have lost just twice across 17 matches in all competitions. So this is a nailed-on Seagulls win, right?
Maybe, though Fabian Hürzeler will be guarding against complacency, especially because Hull have not lost by more than one goal in any game this season and have not conceded more than two. They are the proverbial hard nut to crack, albeit scoring goals is a problem for the Tigers - despite sitting 14th in the table, only two teams (Nottingham Forest and Sunderland) have scored fewer.
Team news has already dropped so we'll bring you that in the next post. Kick-off is at 2pm (GMT) so please do stay tuned. I'm predicting this will be a tighter game than many would imagine.
new_text:
Signing off today's live blog with a link to Aaron Bower's match report from the MKM Stadium. If you can have a smash and grab by a home team, it was most certainly that ... with Konstantinos Tzolakis and Oliver McBurnie the heroes clad in black and amber.
It's a bitter pill for Brighton to swallow; that journey back down to the south coast will be feeling even longer than normal.
Thanks for joining, everyone. Enjoy the rest of your weekends.
Here's what McBurnie has said to Sky Sports after the game:
We haven't lost a game at home. They are a top team and we knew it was going to be tough. We rode our luck and we have the big man [Konstantinos Tzolakis] to keep the ball out of the net so that's what he's done.
He was unbelievable. He has been all season for us to be fair to him. We give him a bit of stick about his gear but he's been good in net. He was fantastic, kept us in the game today. We know if we are always in games we fancy ourselves to get chances and that's what we did today.
If Liverpool versus Manchester United has even a fraction of the excitement of those final few minutes at Hull City, we are all in for a treat this afternoon.
Rob Smyth is all over the updates of English football's biggest fixture.
This is definitely an '... and breathe' situation. I cannot quite believe what we've witnessed in that period of stoppage time.
We'll soon bring you some reaction from both camps, as Hull win 2-0 to maintain their unbeaten home record since promotion and Brighton suffer just their third defeat in all competitions this season.
How on earth this game has ended 2-0 to Hull City is quite unfathomable. Brighton had all the chances, but then it all unravelled for the Seagulls late in the day, first with Costinha's red card and then with a late double from Oliver McBurnie.
Konstantinos Tzolakis also played his part for the Tigers, making a string of brilliant saves, and Fabian Hürzeler is looking rather bemused on the pitch at the end.
90+4 mins: We will get an extra period of added time at the end of this game, I think, because of that goal. Credit to Lucas Gourna-Douath for his role in it, by the way, he linked up nicely with Slater.
What a moment for the Tigers. It was a breakaway, and it was brilliantly worked, first inside to Slater, then out right, and then McBurnie pounced from close range to convert.
All those Brighton chances and then that happens in stoppage time. That's football for you.
A second yellow card has been shown to Costinha for a blatant pull-back on Sorba Thomas. Good work from Thomas to use his body and then go down when feeling the tug. Brighton will finish the game with 10 men, as we approach stoppage time.
87 mins: Persistence from Minteh in making a couple of blocks sees Hull penned in deep in their own half. Is there a late chance coming here for Brighton?
85 mins: To be honest, Brighton's grip on this game has loosened in the past 15 to 20 minutes. It doesn't feel like they are battering down the door to score.
84 mins: There's a cheap concession in the middle of the pitch, which means Brighton can knock it around and keep the pressure on. A final change from Sergej Jakirovic sees Coyle replaced by Brooke Norton-Cuffy.
83 mins: A wild Slater shot hits a big deflection, which is enough for a Hull corner. Is belief growing among the home fans that their team can nick it? Verbruggen tips the corner away and Brighton get a free-kick in the end.
81 mins: Ferdi Kadioglu replaces Diego Gomez as Hürzeler rolls the dice one more time. Gomez could have scored a hat-trick today, yet he trudges off goalless.
80 mins: Off the line by Slater. Was Kostoulas offside anyway? A flag has gone up, but the striker was most definitely onside. Perhaps the flag was for a foul. Yep, Hinshelwood pushed Slater into the post as the Hull player was heading the ball to safety. It's all happening now.
78 mins: Thomas continues to provide a counterattacking threat down Hull's left wing, and there are strong appeals for a handball by the home faithful. I don't think it even struck Dunk's hand, to be honest.
Sorba Thomas has hit the woodwork! I think it was a cross, but no matter his left-footed effort floated over Verbruggen's head and crashes against the crossbar. That would have been pretty crazy.
Unless I'm forgetting someone obvious, Brighton's vaunted scouting methods have never turned up an elite finisher. If they had someone up front that could be relied upon to put away more of the countless chances they create, they'd be running away with the league.
73 mins: Yeah, Brighton haven't really found their rhythm since making the triple change. Kostoulas is making the runs in behind, he just needs to be found.
72 mins: It's become a bit scrappy, which suits Hull just fine, with the hosts still looking pretty sharp and organised in defence, leaping onto the loose balls. A 0-0 would be frustrating in some ways, given how often they draw at home, but it would also represent a solid point against a good team.
Hull have a corner here. Can they produce something unexpected?
Oh my goodness I thought Belloumi had scored! He travelled with the ball so far, carrying it deep into the Brighton box, then cutting inside on his left foot and somehow sliding it way of the near post. He holds his head in his hands.
64 mins: For me, Brighton lack a bit of thrust in the final third so I'd be sending on Minteh and Kostoulas. But that's just me. And I eat Pringles and watch games from my upstairs spare room, while Hürzeler, who is my age, manages Brighton.
63 mins: That's canny play from Thomas, tracking back to nick the ball off Costinha and then forcing the Brighton right-back to foul him. It's a yellow card for Costinha too.
There's very little respite for Hull, though; even when they get the ball forward, it's coming back just as quickly.
61 mins: Rutter teases Coyle on the Brighton left before flashing one across the face of goal. Pretty harmless actually, that one, and the Frenchman cuts a frustrated figure.
